annotation.title_clean: Cloud Robotics Law and Regulation: Challenges in the Governance of Complex and Dynamic Cyber-Physical Ecosystems
annotation.title_en: Cloud Robotics Law and Regulation: Challenges in the Governance of Complex and Dynamic Cyber-Physical Ecosystems
annotation.venue: QMUL Cloud Legal Project / SSRN (Legal Studies Research Paper)
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Legal research paper analysing regulatory challenges where physical robots integrate with cloud services. It maps the fragmented EU framework (product safety, liability, GDPR, standards), examines multi-party responsibility and liability attribution, and data-protection issues such as identifying controllers and processors, transparency and portability.
key_provisions_or_claims: No regulatory framework exists specifically for cloud robotics; a patchwork of EU product safety, liability and data laws applies.
Product liability concepts of product vs service and defect are strained by hardware-software-cloud mixtures.
Attributing responsibility across robot makers, cloud providers and service providers is difficult in multi-party ecosystems.
Balance needed between private standard-setting and public law-making.
GDPR controller/processor identification, transparency and data portability are unclear in cloud robotics.
